What changed in the ledgers since a commit

Source: R/changes.R
changes.Rd

Compares the ledgers of a set-up project in the working tree with those at a git commit, and lists the entries that changed, were added or were removed, the conditions that are new, and the ledgers that are stale (rule 7.3, 7.2.1).

Usage

changes(since = "HEAD", path = ".", files = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'weft_changes'
print(x, brief = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

since

One string naming a commit (anything git rev-parse accepts). "HEAD" in a repository with no commit compares with nothing, so every ledger is new.

path

A folder inside the project; the root is found as elsewhere in weft and must hold _weft.yml.

files

NULL, or source paths relative to the root; only their ledgers are compared.

x

A weft_changes.

brief

If TRUE, print only the header line, the structural changes, the ledgers not re-rendered and the new conditions.

...

Unused.

Value

A weft_changes, a list of the tables entries, conditions, stale, ledgers and findings, with the attributes since, commit (the full hash, or NA) and root. It prints as plain text.

Details

An entry is changed when its text or its arm differs; a different raw value alone is not a change. Changed entries are ranked: those with a structural reason (an arm change, a sign flip, a crossing of 0, 1.0 or a dictionary value, a change of an order of magnitude) first, then those beside a claim word, then by relative change. A ledger is stale when what its header recorded (targets in the store, dictionary entries, source files) differs now, so its entries were not re-rendered.

changes() renders nothing, runs no pipeline and writes nothing. It reads git only. Because it runs no pipeline it does not see a store that is behind its code. findings lists the tier-2 lints of lints() over the lines added since the commit, with the columns file, line, rule and message; a file with more claim-word findings than its claim_cap gets one row that counts them. Ledgers are paired by path; a source that was renamed is paired with the old one when at least half of its entries match and the two output names are equal or each is its own source's base name; a ledger whose source is gone counts as the old one even while it is still in the working tree. Where one expression occurs several times in a section and the counts differ, the occurrences are lined up by their sentences, so a deleted one is reported as removed. Entries of a section whose heading was renamed are paired and marked (section renamed from #old). A threshold from the dictionary that is a quantity is compared in its own unit, using the unit the ledger records beside raw; an entry from an older ledger, or a plain number, gives no such crossing. A note under "Ledgers" says so when git ignores _weft/ledger/ (git check-ignore -q, the only git command added to rev-parse, ls-tree and show).

The claim words are English only, so a chapter in another language gets no claim-word ranking, and the interim list is broad (it holds common words such as no, all and more, but not the number words one to twelve, first, second or third); stage 3's lexicon replaces it. A crossing of 1.0 is a reason only where the entry has no unit on either side (a ratio or a count).

print(x, brief = TRUE) prints the header line, the structural changes, the ledgers not re-rendered and the new conditions, and nothing else.
